partners.mechanism_chain: SMN1 (HGNC:11117) —PRODUCES→ SMN protein (HGNC:11117); SMN protein (HGNC:11117) —DISRUPTS→ snRNP assembly (GO:0000326); snRNP assembly (GO:0000326) —DECREASES→ neuronal function (GO:0050769); neuronal function (GO:0050769) —LEADS_TO→ motor neuron degeneration (HP:0002397); neuronal function (GO:0050769) —LEADS_TO→ muscle atrophy (HP:0003202). Mutations in SMN1 lead to reduced production of functional SMN protein. This impaired SMN protein disrupts the essential process of snRNP assembly, which is crucial for proper neuronal function. partners.mechanism_chain: SMN1 (HGNC:10993) —DISRUPTS→ SMN protein complex assembly and function (GO:0005829); SMN protein complex assembly and function (GO:0005829) —LEADS_TO→ Motor neuron degeneration (HP:0003198); RPS23 (HGNC:10429) —DISRUPTS→ Ribosome biogenesis (GO:0042254); Ribosome biogenesis (GO:0042254) —LEADS_TO→ Protein synthesis (GO:0006412); Protein synthesis (GO:0006412) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263); Protein synthesis (GO:0006412) —LEADS_TO→ Brachycephaly (HP:0000256); Protein synthesis (GO:0006412) —LEADS_TO→ Trichomegaly (HP:0003571); SMN protein complex assembly and function (GO:0005829) —LEADS_TO→ Protein synthesis (GO:0006412). Mutations in SMN1 lead to defects in SMN protein complex assembly and function, which in turn impacts the biogenesis and stability of spliceosomes and snRNPs, ultimately contributing to motor neuron degeneration characteristic of SMA. Concurrently, mutations in RPS23 disrupt ribosome biogenesis, impairing overall protein synthesis. This widespread reduction in protein synthesis, particularly affecting rapidly developing tissues and neurons, underlies the developmental delay, brachycephaly, and trichomegaly seen in BTDD. The convergence is on the critical process of protein synthesis, essential for both neuronal survival and overall development.
